fields.Overview (Player): Caelestis is the spelljammer academy where the cadets train, a layered machine of halls, ranks, and access permissions overlooking the Astral Sea. Led by Mirt, it drills its cadets through simulation and salvage exercise. A wave of thefts continues to spread through the tower, reaching an instructor's own possessions.

bullets: The tower academy where the cadets train, containing the simulation deck, administration, cadet quarters, sky dock, quartermaster's stores, Spelljammer Nexus, and gymnasium
Overlooks the Astral Sea and is organized as a layered order of halls, ranks, and thresholds
Struck by a coordinated wave of burglaries during the attack on Mirt
An arcane device detonated in its simulation chamber, nearly killing a room of cadets
Holds a bridge where Mirt keeps his fishbowl, and an infirmary where the injured recover
Governs a fleet-intelligence archive locked behind clearance beyond a cadet's star

fields.Overview (Player): The Spelljammer Nexus is a training chamber at Caelestis overlooking the Astral Sea, where cadets learn to extend mind and magic into a vessel by guiding miniature ships across a floating field.

bullets: A room overlooking the Astral Sea where cadets guide miniature spelljamming ships over a floating field
The cadets ran their first true helm exercise here under the tension of an ectoplasmic breach elsewhere in the tower
Tarto brought Boogie, Gregory, and Bartholomew here to practice, where Saerthe learned his own miniature ship had been stolen
Bartholomew's ease at the helm here settled the crew's open spelljammer seat
Holds library terminals between the mock helms and Saerthe's cluttered desk
Gregory searched its terminals for arcane artillery and runes but was locked out of a fleet-intelligence archive category by his cadet star

fields.Overview (Player): Mirt's quarters are the cluttered, excess-strewn chambers of Caelestis's head, home to a fishbowl of octopi and an impossible wardrobe that opens onto bounded astral night — a magical replica of a place in the Viren star system.

bullets: Cluttered chambers of Caelestis's head, scattered with clothes, curiosities, and a fishbowl holding two octopi, Flotsam and Jetsam
Contains a wardrobe that opens onto a bounded stretch of astral night with unfamiliar constellations
Site of the fight with the centipede creatures released from the delivered crate

fields.Overview (Player): The sky dock is Caelestis's docking bay beneath the void, where spelljamming ships of every shape rest and cadets learn the anatomy of a vessel and the workings of the helm.

bullets: Where spelljamming ships of every shape rest beneath the void; Kip and Pik taught the cadets the anatomy of a vessel and the meaning of the helm
Boogie noticed a suspicious exchange between a dock officer and a merchant here
Casey came here looking for Joffrey, did not find him, and sat at the rail thinking of his brother when the familiar presence settled beside him again
Boogie and Sol talked past a security guard, invoking Mirt's name, to trace a crate here
They found a crate marked with the rod's symbol tucked behind others, holding something neither living nor hollow
Sol learned from a cargo clerk that shipments route through Mr. Blip, with Toril as the nearest destination and H’Catha a secondary stop

items.name: Marked Crate at the Sky Dock

fields.Overview (Player): The Viren star system, beyond a place called H’Catha, is the region Mirt's impossible wardrobe magically replicates. A vision and a guiding voice have pointed Casey toward it as a destination.

bullets: Named by Mirt as the location, beyond H’Catha, that his wardrobe magically replicates; the destination Casey's vision and guiding voice pointed toward

fields.Overview (Player): The Weeping Goddess is Caelestis's bustling refectory, thronged with cadets from every corner of wildspace beneath blue-glowing orbs. Its kitchen is run by Petty Officer Winston Ryeback, and a back-wall notice board carries odd jobs, dock requests, and missing-item notices.

bullets: Caelestis's crowded refectory, packed with cadets of every wildspace people beneath blue-glowing orbs
Petty Officer Winston Ryeback runs its kitchen at a carrying bellow
Known for its dragon scale pizza and knock-your-mama's-socks-off soup
Along the back wall runs a board of handwritten notices — well-wishes, odd jobs, dock requests, and missing-item notices
Where the crew first gathered as a table and sorted out their shipboard roles

fields.Overview (Player): The Sea Dock is one of Caelestis's docking bays, named on a cargo notice Casey pulled from the refectory board. He meant to work a job here but confused it with a neighboring dock.

bullets: The dock named in a cargo notice Casey pulled from the refectory board
Casey confused it with another dock and ended up working cargo for Rindle Gearloft instead

fields.Key NPCs / Factions: Saerthe Abizjn, Boatswain Tarto, Caelestis Academy
fields.Overview (Player): The Simulation Deck is the chamber at Caelestis where cadets enter pods to run immersive exercises. Here both cadet crews were briefed and set against each other in a salvage race through simulated wildspace.

bullets: Where both cadet crews were summoned and briefed by Saerthe and Tarto for a salvage race
Cadets entered pods here to run the simulation of a hammerhead recovering a logbook from a derelict in an asteroid field

fields.Overview (Player): The Moonraider was Captain Sardax's ship. The crew has been aboard it only in simulation: they woke on its deck in the middle of a losing battle against astral reavers, Sardax bleeding across the planks, until the scene froze and revealed itself as a simulation of her final stand, a test never meant to be won.

bullets: Known to the crew only in simulation, as the ship of Captain Sardax's final stand
The cadets woke on its deck mid-battle as astral reavers swarmed over the rail, explosions tearing through rigging and mast
The scene froze and peeled away, and they woke on the Simulation Deck of Caelestis

fields.Overview (Player): The derelict was the prize of the salvage race, a wreck adrift in an asteroid field, met only in simulation. The crew reached it across a chain of drifting asteroids, and in its captain's quarters found the logbook half-tucked behind the body of something long decomposed.

bullets: Known to the crew only in simulation, as the objective of the salvage race against Miken's crew
Adrift in an asteroid field, reached by leaping between asteroids
Its lower corridors were dark and creaking; the logbook lay in the captain's quarters behind a long-decomposed body
A githyanki vessel closed on it through the asteroids while the crew was aboard

fields.Overview (Player): The tyrant ship is a stone-carved beholder vessel in Toril's orbit, once the vessel of the beholder Vaelorix, who lies dead on its Command Deck. The crew holds it now. They burned the bloom off the Command Deck, put the mechanical behir out through the cargo hold, and seated a helm in the platform so they can fly it through H'Cathan space unnoticed. It flies, though only four of its ten great eyes answer at the crew stations. It has no fire suppression; most things leave it through the cargo hold.

bullets: A stone-carved beholder vessel drifting in orbit above Toril, believed abandoned
The crew was to install a spelljamming helm on its command deck and use its appearance to move through H’Cathan space unchallenged
Its interior is stone-floored, dim, and smells old; a lantern-wisp bloom has overrun much of it
Clockwork horrors were found feeding on the broken automaton Ostekk-6 in the cargo hold
The crew dispatched the clockwork horrors in the cargo hold and cleared the lantern-wisp bloom choking the garden shaft, but found the wisps persisted by some unknown cause
A deck below waits reachable only by rope; the crew held to rest before descending, sensing something waiting there
Has no windows; circling Toril, its hours run close to the academy's
Its decks are joined by shafts once served by a small propulsion system for its units, no longer working
Below the cargo space lie the Hollow Deck and then the Command Deck
Partway down the shaft, a plane where the ship's gravity turns over lies just above the Command Deck
Its master, the beholder Vaelorix, lies dead on the Command Deck
Most things leave the ship through the cargo hold, with the expulsion worked from the Command Deck
Nothing aboard puts out a fire
The crew holds it, and a helm is being fitted on the Command Deck

links.name: The Tyrant Ship and the H’Catha Meteor

fields.Overview (Player): The Flighty Foundling is a Caelestis Academy ship. It carried the crew out from the academy to the tyrant ship above Toril, dropped them into its cargo deck and left. Once the helm was seated it came back to meet them with Saerthe and Boatswain Tarto aboard, easing alongside until the two ships' air envelopes met. It is to carry Pffred and Krik'Lit back to Caelestis.

bullets: Carried the crew from Caelestis to the tyrant ship in orbit above Toril
Dropped them into the tyrant ship's cargo deck and departed
Answered Ryeback's word to Caelestis and came to meet the crew on the third day after the helm was seated
Eased alongside until its air envelope met the tyrant ship's, with Saerthe and Boatswain Tarto at its rail
Is to return Pffred and Krik'Lit to Caelestis, and its crew ran a gangway out between the ships

fields.Overview (Player): H’Catha is a world populated entirely by beholders and their kin, watched by beholder patrols. An adamantine meteor has struck its spire, and the crew has been sent to recover it — using a tyrant ship's appearance to move through H’Cathan space unchallenged.

bullets: Named by Mirt as a place the Viren star system lies beyond
A world populated entirely by beholders and their kin, watched by beholder patrols
Struck by an adamantine meteor that hit its spire, which the crew was sent to recover
Named by a Sky Dock cargo clerk as a secondary destination for certain shipments

links.name: The Tyrant Ship and the H’Catha Meteor

fields.Overview (Player): Toril is a world named as the nearest destination on most of the academy's shipping routes. The tyrant ship the crew boarded, and now holds, drifts in orbit above it.

bullets: Named by a Sky Dock cargo clerk as the nearest destination on most shipping routes
The world above which the abandoned tyrant ship drifts in orbit

links.name: The Tyrant Ship and the H’Catha Meteor

fields.Overview (Player): The system the crew calls home — a sun, a scatter of inner and outer worlds, and the edge where Wildspace begins.

The Hollow Deck lies below the tyrant ship's cargo space: a round, enclosed room shaped like a pit, its walls lined with unfamiliar machinery. It was the ship's deck for repairs and maintenance, with a repair bay on its far side. Its floor is strewn with the torn-apart remains of the ship's automaton units and wrecked clockwork horrors, and three or four dormant horrors stand where the mechanical behir used to lie.

bullets: Reached from the shaft through a side opening carved and scored as if cut through the ship one pass at a time
A round room shaped like a pit, walls lined with machinery, strewn with wrecked units and clockwork horrors
Once the ship's deck for repairs and maintenance, run by Vaelorix, with a repair bay on its far side
A mechanical behir lies coiled beside the repair bay; the crew fought it there and retreated
Passed on the way to the garden, Ostekk-10 curled in its corner with three or four clockwork horrors dormant around it

fields.Overview (Player): The Command Deck lies past the plane where the tyrant ship's gravity turns over. Its flowers made the wisps and the field that killed magic; the crew burned and tore them out, and magic works there again. The beholder Vaelorix lies dead on the helm platform, his central eye dried open, and a helm now sits where he died, with crew stations rigged around it, one for each of the great eyes along the hull. The controls for the ship's expulsion are here.

bullets: Reached through a carved opening just past the plane where the ship's gravity turns over
A large room of drifting colored light, its walls overgrown with flowers, a great dark flower rising from a mound at its center
Clockwork horrors stand frozen mid-stride among the flowers
Magic fails there: the dead beholder at its heart still cancels it with its central eye
Wisps bloom from the flowers and drift toward the living, latching on and draining them
The beholder's body lies on the platform where the helm must go
Spores from the garden flower showed the wisps, and the flowers proved to make both the wisps and the field
The side flowers were cut down one by one, the ceiling flower dropped, and Bartholomew tore the great flower from the body
Magic returned once the flowers fell
The helm was carried here and its fitting begun

links.name: The Tyrant Ship and the H’Catha Meteor

fields.Overview (Player): The garden lies at the bottom of the tyrant ship's garden shaft, where Vaelorix kept his research specimens. It is a lavish greenhouse: cultivated flowers along the walls, a bed of grass at its centre, and research tables laid out with instruments and dissected flowers. A thick stalk of unopened velvet-blue buds stands at the heart of it, and a single whole wisp drifts in the air.

bullets: Reached down the garden shaft on Ostekk-6's directions
A greenhouse of cultivated flowers, a grass bed and research tables
Tumak took a half-dissected flower that glowed pink inside its bud
Bartholomew found a newly bloomed flower whose scent made his body want to change
